text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi got the go-ahead from majority parties to introduce a corrective mini-budget which will include around 16 trillion lire of deficit-cutting measures. Around two-thirds of the deficit-saving measures will come from cuts to unspecified state funds and re-organisation of the tax system. The rest will come from obliging firms to stump up taxes on huge severance payment funds two years ahead of time and by holding back end-of-contract retirement settlements to state workers for six months. The budget package is expected to be approved by the cabinet today (all).

* Hard-left Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti said he had won his battle to prevent any tax hikes or cuts to social spending. Opposition centre-right parties said they were fiercely opposed to the mini-budget and were planning to stage a national demonstration as a sign of protest against the government (all).

* Post and telecommunications minister Antonio Maccanico in an interview says he is ready to resign if its planned reform of Italy's broadcasting system, which is due to be approved by the end of May, is delayed any further (Corriere della Sera).
* Italy's unemployment rate rose to 12.4 percent in January from 12.2 percent a year ago (all).

* Shareholders in state-controlled telecoms holding STET approved the introduction of a so-called golden share to be held by the Treasury in the future privatised group. Shareholders who do not want to keep their shares for a merger with Telecom Italia will be offered 6,466.18 lire per ordinary (all).
* Tyre and cables group Pirelli posted a 43 percent rise in its 1996 net profits, with a doubled dividend and the promise of more to come for 1997 (all).

* The board of textiles group Marzotto presented its 1996 balance sheet and gave its go-ahead to the merger with newly formed company HPI, which was recently spun-off from financial holding Gemina (all).

* 1996 seems to have been a good year for Italy's banks: Credito italiano posted a 43.5 percent rise in its 1996 consolidated net profit, while Banca di Roma profit grew 16.9 percent. Istituto Mobiliare Italiano (IMI) net profit also posted a 20 percent rise (all).
* State-controlled engineering group Finmeccanica will reportedly post a loss of 400 billion lire for 1996 (Sole 24 Ore).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
